entities.summary:
Harpalus was an ancient Greek astronomer who corrected the cycle of Cleostratus and invented the Nine Year Cycle.

Born in the 6th century BCE, Harpalus was a prominent figure in the Hellenistic era, known for his contributions to the field of astronomy.

Harpalus' work built upon the earlier discoveries of Cleostratus, who had identified a cycle of 365.24 days that was close to, but not exact, the Earth's orbital period around the Sun.

Harpalus' innovation led to a more accurate calculation of the solar year, which in turn allowed for more precise predictions of celestial events and the timing of agricultural cycles.

The Nine Year Cycle, also known as the Metonic cycle, was a major breakthrough in astronomical understanding and had a significant impact on the development of Western astronomy.

Harpalus' legacy can be seen in the work of later astronomers, such as Hipparchus and Ptolemy, who built upon his discoveries to further refine our understanding of the universe.

As a testament to his significance, Harpalus is remembered as one of the most important astronomers of the ancient Greek world.

Harpalus' discovery of the Nine Year Cycle is often cited as an example of the power of human curiosity and ingenuity in understanding the workings of the universe.

This achievement has had a lasting impact on our understanding of the solar system and the development of modern astronomy.
